audit.whatIsWrong: Three chart rows give Garen a stage the page's own prose says is even or Swain's: Level 3, Level 6 and First item.
audit.why: whys[2] literally says 'the lane is genuinely even', whys[4] calls level 6 'your one real ownership moment', whys[5] says 'even is the honest call' — yet the sides read Garen, Skill, Garen. The packet chart says Skill, Swain, Skill and the already-audited mirror confirms it.
audit.corrected: win[2]/phases[2].side to Skill, win[4]/phases[4].side to Swain, win[5]/phases[5].side to Skill, with ratings moved to 5/10 to match.

audit.why: Spike order is honest: he owns levels 1-2, you own the level 6 extended-fight window, first item is contested, and the late game is his. Only the wording inside them needed fixing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Decisive Strike is described as cancelling your E 'mid-cast before the hand travels' and as something he 'presses mid-dash', and the early text has you 'arriving rooted without a pull'.
audit.why: Decisive Strike is not a dash and not an instant silence: it is a move-speed burst that empowers his NEXT basic attack, and the silence lands with that attack. The tell is the auto wind-up, not the cast. Swain also has no dash, so 'arrive rooted' is nonsense on his side. A silence prevents new casts; it does not recall a Nevermove wave already in flight, and the root is on that wave's return pass.
audit.corrected: Silence tied to the empowered auto with the wind-up named as the cue to step back; Nevermove described as rooting on the return pass; the false dash removed.
sources: enemyKit Q text and autoReset flag

audit.whatIsWrong: packet defects flag zero cooldown-sequencing advice, and the page has none.
audit.why: Courage runs 22 seconds at rank 1 down to 12 at rank 5 and Decisive Strike is a flat 8; those two numbers decide when a trade is free.
audit.corrected: Both written into mid, keyed to when you may commit.

audit.why: Anti-heal is already core in report[8] and breakdown.late, which is right against Perseverance.

audit.whatIsWrong: Courage is quantified as cutting magic burst by exactly 30%.
audit.why: Riot's text gives a shield with brief tenacity followed by a lesser damage reduction, with no percentage. The number cannot be verified from the kits, and a wrong number is worse than none.
audit.corrected: Described as shield-then-damage-reduction, so the advice (force it out before you commit) survives without an invented figure.

edits.before: His Q silence cancels E mid-cast before the hand travels; trading at Level 2 means eating an empowered strike while your combo fizzles.
edits.after: Decisive Strike silences on his next attack, not on the cast — the wind-up is the tell. Trade at 2 and you eat it with your E locked out.

edits.before: Courage's tenacity cuts your W slow and his passive regen resets between your mana-expensive poke attempts — Garen controls spacing and timing here.
edits.after: Decisive Strike breaks free of every slow you land and Perseverance refills him between your mana-expensive pokes, so he picks when trades start and when they end.

edits.before: Shadowflame/Luden's spike is real but Courage absorbs 30% of the burst and his Q silence still shuts down your combo if he catches you first — even is the honest call.
edits.after: Your first-item spike is real, but Courage shields the burst and leaves damage reduction behind, and one silence still ends your combo if he lands it first — even is honest.

edits.before: Garen's Q silence cancels your E mid-cast and his passive regen erases your early poke before you have W — he controls this window completely.
edits.after: Decisive Strike's silence arrives on his next attack and Perseverance erases your poke before you even have W — he owns this window completely.

edits.before: Shadowflame or Luden's makes your W poke genuinely threatening, but Garen's W (Courage) cuts magic burst by 30% and his silence still deletes your combo setup if he catches you.
edits.after: Shadowflame or Luden's makes your poke genuinely threatening, but Courage shields the burst and leaves damage reduction behind, and his silence still deletes the combo if he lands it.

edits.before: At Level 1 you have no root and no silence answer — Garen's Q cancels any cast it touches, and his passive regen outheals your Q poke if he disengages behind minions. Do not trade at Level 1; last-hit at W range and accept a free early. Level 2 is marginally better but Garen's Q silence specifically deletes your E combo window: he presses Q mid-dash and you arrive rooted without a pull, having eaten an empowered strike for nothing. At Level 3 the W-slow is the only safe poke tool — drop W at max range to clip him while he spins, then disengage before his Q comes back up. You are not winning this level band, you are surviving it with fragments.
edits.after: At Level 1 you have no root and no answer to a silence — Decisive Strike empowers his next attack, and Perseverance outheals your poke the moment he steps behind minions. Do not trade; last-hit from range and accept a quiet start. Level 2 is barely better, because that silence is aimed at your E window: he walks up, the auto wind-up lands, and you stand there with Nevermove locked out and an empowered strike taken for nothing. Step back on the wind-up, not on the cast. At Level 3 Vision of Empire is your safe poke — drop it at max range to clip him while he spins, then leave before his Q returns on its flat 8 seconds. You are not winning this band, you are banking fragments through it.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are Garen's strongest sustained pressure: he has his full kit, his Courage passive tenacity reduces your W slow's effectiveness, and your mana costs are punishing if you fish for E roots he can simply Q-cancel. The moment he hits you with Q while you have E primed, the combo is dead. At Level 6 your R changes the calculus in one specific way — if you have landed even two successful E-root-pulls beforehand and have meaningful fragment stacks, your drain sustain outlasts his Courage window and spin damage in a prolonged fight. But you must force that extended fight: short trades still favor him because Q silence disrupts your Demonflare timing and Courage eats the nova burst.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are Garen's strongest stretch: full kit, Decisive Strike shedding every slow you land on its flat 8 seconds, and mana costs that punish you for fishing roots he can silence you out of. The moment that empowered attack lands with E primed, the combo is dead. At Level 6 your R changes one specific thing — with fragments banked and a root or two already landed, your drain outlasts both his spin and his Courage, which is only up every 22 seconds at rank 1 and still 12 when maxed. Force the extended fight inside that gap: short trades favour him, because one silence breaks your Demonflare timing and the shield swallows the nova.
